title: Compliance change and verification
audience: Any owner or compliance contact in any service business who must keep the business's rules, licences and policies current.
learningOutcomes: Describe a process for finding and recording changes to the rules that apply to the business.
Verify that the business's licences, registrations, insurance and policies are current.
Update the procedures and tell the team when a rule changes.

instruction.heading: Find the change
instruction.body: Rules that apply to a service business change. Licences are renewed or reclassified, councils change local laws, state regulators issue new guidance, and national model laws are adopted in some states and not others. Set a regular check, such as monthly for licences and insurance and quarterly for rules and guidance, and record each check. Use the official source for each rule, and record the source, the URL and the date checked. A change reported in a newsletter or a forum must be confirmed against the official source before the business acts on it.

instruction.heading: Verify and record
instruction.body: Verify that each licence, registration, permit and insurance policy is current, that the holder is the person doing the work, and that the scope of the licence covers the work. Record the expiry date and set a reminder before renewal. Where a rule changes, record what changed, when it takes effect, which procedures are affected and who must be told. A change that takes effect in the future, such as a changed exposure limit list, must be planned before the date.

instruction.heading: Update and tell the team
instruction.body: Update the affected procedures, checklists and training, and tell the team and any subcontractor what has changed and when it takes effect. Record that the update was made and that the team was told. Keep the old version of the procedure for the period of the change, so that work done before the change can be checked against the rule that applied at the time.

procedure: Set a regular check for licences, insurance, rules and guidance, and record each check.
Confirm each change against the official source, and record the source, URL and date checked.
Verify each licence, registration and insurance policy is current and covers the work.
Record the change, its effective date, the affected procedures and who must be told.
Update the procedures, checklists and training before the effective date.
Tell the team and subcontractors, and record that they were told.

workedExamples.situation: A team member sees a social media post saying a rule for a chemical has changed from next month.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not act on the post. Check the official regulator source for the change, its effective date and its scope. Record the source and the date checked. If confirmed, plan the procedure update before the effective date and tell the team.

commonErrors.error: Acting on a rule change reported on social media or in a forum.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm every change against the official source and record the date checked.

commonErrors.error: Letting a licence or insurance policy expire without a reminder.
commonErrors.prevention: Record expiry dates and set reminders before renewal.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WorkSafe Victoria states that from 1 December 2026, Safe Work Australia replaces the Workplace Exposure Standards list with the Workplace Exposure Limits list. This is an example of a rule change that must be planned for before its effective date.
Licence renewal, insurance expiry and changes in licence scope must be verified before work is accepted. This lesson does not grant any licence or extend any licence scope.

qualityStandard: Each regulatory check is recorded with the source, the URL and the date checked.
Every licence, registration and insurance policy has an expiry date and a renewal reminder.
Every rule change is planned, communicated and recorded before its effective date.
documentationEvidence: Compliance register with the sources, the check dates and the expiry dates.
Change record showing the rule, the effective date, the procedures updated and the team told.
summary: Check rules and licences on a schedule, and confirm each change from the official source.
Record expiry dates and renew before they lapse.
Plan and communicate each change before its effective date, and keep the old procedure for the period of change.

knowledgeChecks.question: A rule change is reported on social media. What should you do first?
options: Update the procedures straight away and tell the team by text.
Confirm the change against the official source and record the date checked.
Pass it on to customers as it is, since they may ask them about it on the day.

knowledgeChecks.question: A licence expires next month. What is the correct action?
options: Wait for it to expire and then renew and carry on with the job
Keep working as before until someone notices and the client has not asked
Record the expiry date and renew it before it lapses, with a reminder set.

knowledgeChecks.question: When a rule changes, who does the lesson say must be told?
options: The team and any subcontractor, of what has changed and when it takes effect

officialReferences.title: Hazardous substances (WorkSafe Victoria)
officialReferences.covers: Read through a summary tool (WebFetch). States that from 1 December 2026 Safe Work Australia replaces the Workplace Exposure Standards list with the Workplace Exposure Limits list. Gives no further detail of the change and says the Workplace Exposure Limits list is published by Safe Work Australia. Publisher: WorkSafe Victoria.
